explanation.text:
The study of truth commended. God must be feared, honored, and trusted, and filial submission, under chastisement, exhibited. The excellence of wisdom urged and illustrated by its place in the divine counsels. Piety enforced by a contrast of the destiny of the righteous and the wicked. (Pro. 3:1-35)

law [and] commandments--all divine instructions (see on Psa 119:1 and Psa 119:4).

let thine heart keep--or sincerely observe (Pro 4:13; Pro 5:2).

bsb.text: My son, do not forget my teaching, but let your heart keep my commandments;

explanation.text:
length . . . life--often promised as blessings (Psa 21:4; Psa 91:16).

peace--includes prosperity (Psa 125:5).

add--abound to thee.

bsb.text: for they will add length to your days, years and peace to your life.

explanation.text:
mercy and truth--God's faithfulness to His promises is often expressed by these terms (Psa 25:10; Psa 57:3). As attributes of men, they express integrity in a wide sense (Pro 16:6; Pro 20:28).

bind . . . write . . . heart--outwardly adorn and inwardly govern motives.

bsb.text: Never let loving devotion or faithfulness leave you; bind them around your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart.

explanation.text:
favour--grace, amiability (Pro 22:11; Psa 45:2); united with this,

a good understanding--(Compare Margin), a discrimination, which secures success.

in the sight . . . man--such as God and man approve.

bsb.text: Then you will find favor and high regard in the sight of God and man.

explanation.text: Trust . . . heart--This is the center and marrow of true wisdom (Pro 22:19; Pro 28:25). The positive duty has its corresponding negation in the admonition against self-confidence.

bsb.text: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding;

explanation.text:
ways-- (Psa 1:1).

acknowledge--by seeking His wise aid (Pro 16:3; Psa 37:5; Jer 9:23-24).

direct--literally, "make plain" (compare Heb 12:13).

bsb.text: in all your ways acknowledge Him, and He will make your paths straight.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 27:2; Rom 12:16).

fear . . . evil--reverentially regarding His law.

bsb.text: Be not wise in your own eyes; fear the LORD and turn away from evil.

explanation.text:
It--This conduct.

health--(Compare Margin).

to thy navel--for all the organs of nourishment.

marrow--(Compare Margin).

bones--frame of body. True piety promotes bodily health.

bsb.text: This will bring healing to your body and refreshment to your bones.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 11:25; Exo 23:19; Deu 18:4; Isa 32:8; Co2 9:13).

bsb.text: Honor the LORD with your wealth and with the firstfruits of all your crops;

explanation.text: presses--or wine fats (Joe 2:24; Joe 3:13).

bsb.text: then your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new wine.

explanation.text: The true intent of afflictions considered; they do not contradict the assertion of the blessed state of the pious (Job 5:17; Heb 12:5-6).

bsb.text: My son, do not reject the discipline of the LORD, and do not loathe His rebuke;

explanation.text: he delighteth--or receiveth as denoting reconciliation regarding the offense which produced chastisement.

bsb.text: for the LORD disciplines the one He loves, as does a father the son in whom he delights.

explanation.text:
findeth--literally, "reaches," or "obtains by seeking."

getteth--literally, "draws out," as metals by digging.

bsb.text: Blessed is the man who finds wisdom, the man who acquires understanding,

explanation.text:
The figure of Pro 3:13 carried out.

it--that is, wisdom.

merchandise of silver--acquisition by trading.

fine gold--dug gold, solid as a nugget.

bsb.text: for she is more profitable than silver, and her gain is better than fine gold.

explanation.text: rubies--gems, or pearls.

bsb.text: She is more precious than rubies; nothing you desire compares with her.

explanation.text: Wisdom personified as bringing the best blessings (compare Mat 6:33; Ti1 4:8).

bsb.text: Long life is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor.

explanation.text: Her ways--such as she directs us to take.

bsb.text: All her ways are pleasant, and all her paths are peaceful.

explanation.text:
Wisdom allegorized as

a tree of life-- (Gen 2:9; Gen 3:22) whose fruit preserves life, gives all that makes living a blessing.

bsb.text: She is a tree of life to those who embrace her, and those who lay hold of her are blessed.

explanation.text: The place of wisdom in the economy of creation and providence commends it to men, who, in proportion to their finite powers, may possess this invaluable attribute, and are thus encouraged by the divine example of its use to seek its possession.

bsb.text: The LORD founded the earth by wisdom and established the heavens by understanding.

explanation.text:
By his knowledge the depths are broken up,.... From whence fountains and rivers flow, and whereby that great cavity was made which holds that large confluence of waters called the sea, Genesis 1:9. Some refer this to the breaking up the fountains of the great deep at the flood, Genesis 7:11; and others to the dividing of the waters of the Red sea when Israel came out of Egypt, Psalm 78:13; all wonderful works of divine wisdom, and show the greatness of him, in whom are "hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge", Colossians 2:3, by whom they were done;

and the clouds drop down the dew; which makes the earth fruitful, and is put for all the blessings of nature, Genesis 27:28; the drops of dew are begotten by the Lord, they have no other father but him; the vanities of the Gentiles cannot produce them; he who fills the clouds with them, from whence they descend, is no other than the mighty God; and such is Christ the Wisdom of God. Some understand this in a mystical sense of Gospel ministers, and of the dew of Gospel doctrine, dropped and distilled by them under the influence and direction of Christ; see Deuteronomy 32:2; but the literal sense is best.

bsb.text: By His knowledge the watery depths were broken open, and the clouds dripped with dew.

explanation.text:
sound wisdom--(compare Pro 2:7).

let . . . eyes--that is, these words of instruction.

bsb.text: My son, do not lose sight of this: Preserve sound judgment and discernment.

explanation.text: assign reasons in their value for happiness and ornament, guidance and support in dangers, both when waking and sleeping.

bsb.text: They will be life to your soul and adornment to your neck.

explanation.text:
Then shall thou walk in thy way safely,.... In the way of thy duty and business, without fear of any enemy; having in sight the Captain of salvation gone before, and walking in such ways of pleasantness and peace as Wisdom's are; and having such a lamp to the feet, and such a light unto the paths, as the Gospel and its doctrines be;

and thy foot shall not stumble; at the word and the truths of it, as some men do, being thereunto appointed; and at Christ, the stumbling stone laid in Zion, particularly at his justifying righteousness; see 1 Peter 2:8.

bsb.text: Then you will go on your way in safety, and your foot will not stumble.

explanation.text:
When thou liest down thou shalt not be afraid,.... That is, when thou liest down on thy bed at night in order to take sleep, having committed thyself into the hands of a faithful Creator and covenant God and Father, and of Christ the Redeemer and Wisdom of God; thou shalt not be afraid of thieves breaking in to hurt thy person or rob thee of thy property, or of fire to consume thy dwelling and substance, and of nocturnal apparitions and diabolical spectres deceiving thy sight and disturbing thy mind: or when thou art "asleep", for so the word also signifies; thou shall not be surprised out of it with any of the above things, or terrified in it with uneasy imaginations, anxious cares, and distressing dreams;

yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be sweet; free of all uneasy thoughts and cares, sound and refreshing, pleasant and comfortable, like that of the labouring man, Ecclesiastes 5:12; see Psalm 4:8. This epithet of "sweet" is often given to "sleep" in poetic writings.

bsb.text: When you lie down, you will not be afraid; when you rest, your sleep will be sweet.

explanation.text:
Be not--or, "You shall not be."

sudden fear--what causes it (Pro 1:27), any unlooked-for evil (Psa 46:3; Psa 91:12; Pe1 3:14).

desolation-- (Pro 1:27).

bsb.text: Do not fear sudden danger or the ruin that overtakes the wicked,

explanation.text:
The reason; such as are objects of God's favor.

be thy confidence--literally, "in thy confidence," in the source of thy strength (compare Nah 3:9, for the same construction, Hebrew).

bsb.text: for the LORD will be your confidence and will keep your foot from the snare.

explanation.text: Promptly fulfil all obligations both of justice and charity (compare Jam 2:15-16).

bsb.text: Do not withhold good from the deserving when it is within your power to act.

explanation.text:
Say not unto thy neighbour,.... Either to whom thou art indebted, and who comes for the payment of a just debt; or to any poor and indigent person that applies for alms:

go, and come again, and tomorrow I will give; go home, and come tomorrow, and I will pay thee what I owe thee; or do not trouble me now, come another time, and perhaps I may relieve thy wants: this should not be said, because a man cannot be sure of tomorrow that he shall ever see it; nor may it be in the power of his hands, should he live unto the morrow, to do as he promises; his substance may be taken from him; and besides, in the mean time, the poor object may perish for want of relief;

when thou hast it by thee; money to pay thy debts with, or to give alms to the poor; and therefore should give readily and at once, and not make any excuses and delays; "bis dat, qui cito dat". Some make this to be part of the covetous man's words, saying, "and there is with thee"; or thou hast enough, thou hast no need to ask of me; thou hast what thou askest; thou art not in want; thou art richer than I; but the other sense is best. The Septuagint and Arabic versions add,

"for thou knowest not what the day following may bring forth;''

or may happen on it.

bsb.text: Do not tell your neighbor, “Come back tomorrow and I will provide”—when you already have the means.

explanation.text: Do not abuse confidence and avoid litigation.

bsb.text: Do not devise evil against your neighbor, for he trustfully dwells beside you.

explanation.text:
Strive not with a man without cause, Either by words, in a wrangling, quarrelsome, and contentious way, for mere trifles; when there is no foundation for it, no just reason given to form a complaint, or pick a quarrel upon; or by deeds, by lawsuits, when there is nothing to proceed upon; or it is so trifling, that it is not worth while to litigate it or contend about: such, who strive either way, are far from following the example of Wisdom or Christ, and from taking his advice, Matthew 12:19;

if he have done thee no harm; no real hurt to thy person, nor injury to thy substance; if he has not abused nor defrauded thee, nor taken any thing from thee by force or fraud, nor withheld from thee what is thy right and due. But otherwise the laws of God and man ought to take place; right may be sought for, and justice should be done.

bsb.text: Do not accuse a man without cause, when he has done you no harm.

explanation.text: oppressor--or man of mischief. The destiny of successful evildoers warns against desiring their lot (Psa 37:1-2, Psa 37:35-36).

bsb.text: Do not envy a violent man or choose any of his ways;

explanation.text:
Reasons for the warning.

froward-- (Pro 2:15).

secret . . . righteous--in their communion (Amo 3:7).

bsb.text: for the LORD detests the perverse, but He is a friend to the upright.

explanation.text: curse . . . wicked--It abides with them, and will be manifested.

bsb.text: The curse of the LORD is on the house of the wicked, but He blesses the home of the righteous.

explanation.text: The retribution of sinners, as in Psa 18:26.

bsb.text: He mocks the mockers, but gives grace to the humble.

explanation.text:
inherit--as a portion.

shame--or disgrace, as opposed to honor.

promotion--(Compare Margin); as honor for well-doing makes men conspicuous, so fools are signalized by disgrace.

bsb.text: The wise will inherit honor, but fools are held up to shame.
